article.name: CowAgent
article.summary: CowAgent is an open-source personal AI assistant and agent harness with a three-stage long-term memory flow: conversation context is summarized into dated Markdown files, then Deep Dream distills daily material into MEMORY.md and a diary. Retrieval combines FTS5 keyword search and embeddings. This review is pinned to the verified current master head; no system, tests, or benchmarks were run.

who_what.text: CowAgent is an open-source personal AI assistant and agent harness. Its memory subsystem complements the broader conversation, tools, skills, and knowledge-base features.

The official repository page identifies master as the default branch. Its master Atom feed reports the full current head 7e7f68e8e3a6a53cf92852f12c2cc5499c7586cd and update time 2026-11-25T09:41:50Z; the official commit page is pinned to that head.

architecture.text: The documented long-term memory is workspace-file based: short-term conversation context is summarized into dated daily Markdown files; Deep Dream distills those files into a concise MEMORY.md and writes a dated dream diary. MEMORY.md is injected into each conversation, while historical daily material is retrieved on demand.

The inspected storage implementation separately models searchable chunks in SQLite. A chunk carries an identifier, user ID, scope, source kind, path, start/end line, text, optional embedding, content hash, and optional metadata. Storage provides FTS5 keyword search and a vector backend; this lower-level index representation should not be conflated with the Markdown files described as durable memory.

The docs describe automatic writes on context trimming, a nightly summary at 23:55, and emergency summarization after model context overflow. Daily summarization and Deep Dream run asynchronously; scheduled distillation follows the completed daily flush.

The workspace is configurable (default ~/cow). The broader README says team agents have their own memory, capabilities, knowledge, and workspace. At the inspected level, this is a workspace and record-scope model; the reviewed sources do not establish a deployment-wide tenant authorization guarantee.

behavior.text: Write: when turn/token limits trim a conversation, the discarded portion is summarized by an LLM and appended to that date's daily memory; the summary is also injected into the retained context asynchronously. The scheduled summary is skipped when there is no changed content, and an API overflow triggers an emergency save. The agent can also use tools to read and write workspace memory.

Update/consolidation: Deep Dream reads current MEMORY.md plus the selected daily memory, asks an LLM to deduplicate, merge, prune, and extract information, then overwrites MEMORY.md and writes a narrative diary. The documented rule gives newer information precedence when it contradicts an older entry. This is whole-file distillation, not a visible per-fact revision or correction ledger.

Delete: the inspected memory guides describe file browsing and memory clearing for short-term session context, but do not specify a long-term memory erasure API or a guaranteed removal procedure across daily files, MEMORY.md, dream diaries, indexes, and backups. The long-term files can be managed in the configured workspace; completeness of any manual deletion was not tested.

Retrieval: the agent can retrieve historical memory with a hybrid keyword (SQLite FTS5/BM25) and embedding-based vector search. The docs describe rank normalization and weighted fusion (default 0.7 vector / 0.3 keyword), a 30-day half-life for daily memory and no decay for core memory. Optional local reranking is off by default. The core MEMORY.md is injected directly; daily material is retrieved as needed.

Scope isolation: the memory chunk model includes user_id and scope fields, and the README describes per-agent workspaces. These are implementation signals for separating records and files, but this review did not verify all search paths, identity propagation, workspace permissions, or cross-agent isolation under adversarial conditions.

Provenance/evidence: indexed chunks retain source kind, file path, line range, content hash, user/scope, and optional metadata, which can locate the stored text. The inspected documentation does not describe claim-level citations, truth/confidence states, or an audit trail connecting a correction to a superseded fact. A dream diary records consolidation changes narratively, rather than as a structured mutation ledger.

Efficiency and observability: bounded context trimming, chunking, hybrid search, daily decay, and optional reranking provide tunable ways to control prompt size and retrieval. The memory page exposes workspace files and dream diaries in the web console; context commands expose context statistics and clear/compact actions. The docs warn that Agent mode uses substantially more tokens than regular chat. No latency, token, cost, or storage measurements were collected for this review.

limits.text: This is a selected source and documentation review at the verified master head. It inspected the README, long-term memory, Deep Dream, and short-term context guides, plus the memory storage, manager, service, and vector backend files. It did not inspect every agent tool call path, workspace permission rule, migration, or integration.

The durable memory flow depends on LLM summaries and consolidation. The docs describe deduplication and conflict handling but provide no adjudicated accuracy results; chained summarization may lose details, and the review did not test for omissions or invented summaries.

The inspected material does not settle long-term deletion completeness, cross-agent isolation, recovery/backup behavior, index rebuild effects, or performance under large corpora and concurrent writes. These require further implementation review and/or a controlled runtime evaluation.

benchmark.note: No CowAgent runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run. Source inspection and documentation are not benchmark results.
